concepts.def: Influential German art school 1919-1933 unifying art, craft, and technology.
Architect (1883-1969) who founded the Bauhaus in Weimar 1919.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gropius founded the Bauhaus in Weimar in April 1919, merging art and applied art schools. The manifesto called for unifying craft and art in a new architecture of the future.
In 1925 the school moved to Dessau. Gropius designed a flat-roofed glass-and-steel building, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Teachers included Kandinsky, Klee, Mies van der Rohe.
After 1933, exiled Bauhaus members shaped American design and architecture: Mies in Chicago, Gropius at Harvard, Albers at Yale. The Bauhaus legacy underpins modernism worldwide.
